title: They can establish a strong early scoring position
observation: Blue opens with calls to take buildings ahead of the moving circle, leads 25-0-3 at 10:00 and reaches 67-18-19 by 35:00.
interpretation: Black Sails can turn early positioning into substantial score. Their later loss should not obscure that opening threat.
response: Contest the next covered building and their route ahead of the circle early; keep an alternative scoring plan if the first approach is lost.
limitation: The exact contribution of each building, role or call is not isolated.

title: Movement calls do not reliably produce one coordinated crossing
observation: The caller repeatedly orders a westward move behind a tank. The 14-16 minute sequence shows a crossing followed by downed states and a reset; comms later criticise too few people moving at the call.
interpretation: The gap between the intended rotation and actual group arrival creates a window to gatekeep the next position.
response: Prepare crossfire on the next exit before the full group arrives. For PHNT, define the release point, smoke owner and ready check so the first few do not cross alone.
limitation: The caller's estimate of how many seconds earlier would have worked is not treated as a measured counterfactual.

title: FOB defence consumes visibility, supply and anti-air attention
observation: The base sequence shows low protective walls and limited views. Comms request jump-ups, report air harassment, discuss fuel shortage and repeatedly return to rebuilding or defending the FOB.
interpretation: Cover is not enough by itself: the position requires observation angles, anti-air and a sustainable support loop while infantry still needs to score.
response: Combine pressure from high ground with attacks on resupply, then watch whether the field group is recalled. PHNT should assign an overwatch and anti-air owner during construction.
limitation: Reported shortages and air pressure are not a complete supply audit; individual enemy assets are not assigned to a member clan.

title: A disabled APC interrupts the reinforcement option
observation: At 67:00 the deployment UI reads radar destroyed, awaiting repairs. Later comms call the APC held hostage and explicitly request destroying their own vehicle to recover access.
interpretation: Denying radar while leaving the vehicle alive can create a more persistent reinforcement problem than a simple combat death.
response: Protect the APC antenna and withdrawal route, carry repair capability and assign recovery before committing the last transport option. Test denial timing in scrims.
limitation: The UI is direct evidence; the exact duration, enemy intent and respawn mechanics are not fully measured.

title: Pull timing can conflict with the regroup order
observation: At about 68 minutes comms explicitly criticise a tower pull after a no-pull order. At 80 minutes another call is clarified as a question rather than an instruction.
interpretation: Ambiguous call authority can make the scoring situation change before the group is ready.
response: Apply pressure while they regroup, but do not depend on a mistake recurring. For PHNT, require one named caller and a clear acknowledgement before the pull.
limitation: The reported lost circle/FOB sequence is comms interpretation, not proof that one action alone caused both losses.

title: They also recognise the antenna-denial tactic
observation: After suffering their own APC issue, Blue explicitly requests the enemy antenna destroyed and tells players not to destroy the APC itself.
interpretation: Expect them to target reinforcement access deliberately, not only chase vehicle kills.
response: Keep your repair and recovery plan ready even if the hull survives. Scout the enemy infantry near the disabled vehicle before sending a mechanic.
limitation: The order is explicit, but successful lasting denial of the enemy spawn is not independently confirmed.

title: The survival finish almost recovers another game
observation: Blue asks for smoke, revives and bodies staying in the zone. From 91 at 89:00 it reaches 99; both Blue and Green are on 99 at 95:15, then Green wins 100-99.
interpretation: This repeats the closing emphasis from the first Black Sails report, but the outcome shows it is conditional on actually sustaining enough presence and access.
response: Contest safe bodies and return routes to the very last point. Do not assume the large earlier deficit or a single late death settles the match.
limitation: The recovery and loss are direct; no exact causal value is assigned to the final revives or spawns.

title: Red contests a predicted route before Blue reaches it
observation: Around 40:30 Blue calls off a fight with two Reds in the woods and acknowledges they were already waiting near the expected route by the barrier.
interpretation: Merciless presents a local route-denial threat rather than only defending the obvious base entrance.
response: Scout one transition ahead and preserve an alternate route. Use a small probe before committing the massed rotation.
limitation: Enemy planning and full unit size are unknown; this does not establish a permanent Merciless habit.

title: Green converts the late scoring opportunity
observation: Green advances from 76 at 75:00 to 93 at 89:00 and 97 at 91:00. After a 99-99 contest it completes the winning point.
interpretation: The combined BNT / Defcon III side remains a late threat despite Blue's early lead and recovery.
response: Track Green alongside the immediate Red firefight. Reserve a way to contest Green's late hold and reinforcement pressure.
limitation: Direct outcome evidence; the member clan, exact final scorer and hidden decision sequence are not separable.
